claim: Acute IAV infection results in an influx of monocytes and DCs to the nasopharynx.
source: Therefore, our data show that acute IAV infection results in an influx of monocytes and DCs to the nasopharynx.

claim: CMs were the most frequent monocytes in blood in both patients and HCs, and remained comparable.
source: As expected, CMs were the most frequent monocytes in blood in both patients and HCs, and remained comparable.

claim: In the nasopharynx of IAV patients as compared to HCs, blood CM frequencies were significantly increased.

claim: IM frequencies were significantly elevated, in both blood and NPA of IAV patients.

claim: Blood NCM appeared to be lower in patients compared to HCs.

claim: During acute IAV infection, all DC subsets were significantly decreased in the blood of patients.

claim: In the nasopharynx, cDC2, cDC1, and PDC frequencies were significantly higher in IAV patients compared to HCs.

evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2E–H.

claim: There is a negative correlation between age of IAV patients and IM frequency in blood (R=–0.55, p=0.0008).
source: We also compared the frequency of IMs in blood and nasopharynx with the age of IAV patients and found a negative correlation in blood (R=–0.55, p=0.0008) (Figure 2H) but a positive correlation in the nasopharynx (R=0.46, p=0.045) (Figure 2I).

claim: There is a positive correlation between age of IAV patients and IM frequency in the nasopharynx (R=0.46, p=0.045).
source: We also compared the frequency of IMs in blood and nasopharynx with the age of IAV patients and found a negative correlation in blood (R=–0.55, p=0.0008) (Figure 2H) but a positive correlation in the nasopharynx (R=0.46, p=0.045) (Figure 2I).

claim: There is an inverse correlation between age and the frequency of cDC2s in NPA (R=–0.558, p=0.016) in IAV patients.

claim: Frequencies of CMs (in blood), IMs (blood and NPA), and cDC2s (blood) in convalescent individuals were reduced and closer to values seen in HCs.

claim: Acute IAV infection resulted in altered monocyte distribution, in particular at the site of infection and was more pronounced in older patients.
source: Acute IAV infection resulted in altered monocyte distribution, in particular at the site of infection and was more pronounced in older patients.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data on monocyte distribution and age correlations.

claim: In IAV patients, monocytes and DCs in the nasopharynx expressed higher levels of HLA-DR than those in blood.
source: In contrast, in IAV patients, monocytes and DCs in the nasopharynx expressed higher levels of HLA-DR than those in blood (Figure 3A and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3A and C.

claim: In IAV patients, nasopharyngeal cDC2s, and cDC1s expressed more CD86 than cells in blood.
source: We also found that in IAV patients, nasopharyngeal cDC2s, and cDC1s expressed more CD86 than cells in blood (Figure 3D), while nasopharyngeal PDCs showed significant upregulation of CD83 during IAV infection as compared to blood PDCs (Figure 3E).

claim: Nasopharyngeal PDCs showed significant upregulation of CD83 during IAV infection as compared to blood PDCs.

evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: There is a significant inverse correlation (R=–0.696, p=0.0019) between CM maturation (CD86 expression) and viral RNA load (Ct values).
source: When we compared maturation of CM and cDCs (i.e., CD86 expression) with viral RNA load (i.e., cycle threshold [Ct] values – number of cycles required to amplify viral RNA), we observed a significant inverse correlation (R=–0.696, p=0.0019), implying that higher viral RNA loads (low Ct value) were associated with increased maturation of CMs (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis and data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Higher viral RNA loads (low Ct value) were associated with increased maturation of CMs.
source: When we compared maturation of CM and cDCs (i.e., CD86 expression) with viral RNA load (i.e., cycle threshold [Ct] values – number of cycles required to amplify viral RNA), we observed a significant inverse correlation (R=–0.696, p=0.0019), implying that higher viral RNA loads (low Ct value) were associated with increased maturation of CMs (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the correlation data.

claim: There is a positive correlation between CD86 expression on nasopharyngeal CMs and nasopharyngeal cDC2s (R=0.735, p=0.0012).
source: We also observed a positive correlation between CD86 expression on nasopharyngeal CMs, and both nasopharyngeal cDC2s (R=0.735, p=0.0012) and cDC1s (R=0.832, p=0.0001) (Figure 3G and H, respectively).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis and data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: There is a positive correlation between CD86 expression on nasopharyngeal CMs and nasopharyngeal cDC1s (R=0.832, p=0.0001).

evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis and data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: In patients with greater viral RNA load who also have more mature CMs in the nasopharynx, there is a greater likelihood of finding mature MDCs in the nasopharynx as well.

evidence: This is an interpretation of the correlation data between CM and MDC maturation.

claim: Elevated levels of TNFα, IL-6, and IFNα were observed in nasopharyngeal secretions of IAV patients as compared to HCs.

evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4A–C and citations to previous studies.

claim: Elevated levels of TNFα, IL-6, and IFNα were observed in plasma of IAV patients as compared to HCs.
source: In agreement with earlier reports (Cole et al., 2017; Oshansky et al., 2014; Gill et al., 2008; Gill et al., 2005), we observed elevated levels of TNFα, IL-6, and IFNα in nasopharyngeal secretions (Figure 4A–C) as well as in plasma of IAV patients as compared to HCs (Figure 4D–F).

claim: There is a positive correlation between soluble TNFα and CM frequency in blood of IAV patients.

claim: There is a positive correlation between soluble TNFα and CM frequency in the nasopharynx of IAV patients.

claim: There are positive associations between age and level of TNFα in plasma and NPA in IAV patients.

claim: Plasma IFNα levels were positively correlated with Ct value (suggesting inverse correlation with viral RNA load).

claim: Patients with higher viral RNA loads had lower amounts of IFNα in circulation.

claim: CCL2 plays a role in the changes to the IMs during infection.

claim: During IAV infection, mature monocytes and DCs accumulate in the nasopharynx.
source: In summary, our data suggest that during IAV infection, mature monocytes and DCs accumulate in the nasopharynx, and blood monocytes and DCs function as a general source of TNFα, potentially contributing to the systemic inflammatory effects accompanying influenza infections.

claim: Blood monocytes and DCs function as a general source of TNFα, potentially contributing to the systemic inflammatory effects accompanying influenza infections.

claim: In blood, three subsets of monocytes are found: the CD14+CD16– classical monocytes (CMs), the most frequent subset at steady state; the terminally differentiated CD14–CD16+ nonclassical monocytes (NCMs); and CD14+CD16+ intermediate monocytes (IMs) that represent CMs transitioning into NCMs.
source: In blood, three subsets of monocytes are found: the CD14+CD16– classical monocytes (CMs), the most frequent subset at steady state; the terminally differentiated CD14–CD16+ nonclassical monocytes (NCMs); and CD14+CD16+ intermediate monocytes (IMs) that represent CMs transitioning into NCMs (Boyette et al., 2017; Jakubzick et al., 2013; Patel et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Few studies compare responses between blood and the nasopharynx in human infections.

claim: Evidence of DC mobilization to the nasal cavity has been reported during IBV and RSV infections.

claim: DC3 may be depleted during severe infection.
source: From later reports establishing DC3 as a distinct DC subset arising from a specific progenitor (Bourdely et al., 2020; Cytlak et al., 2020; Dutertre et al., 2019), especially those describing dysregulated immune responses during SARS-CoV-2 infection (Winheim et al., 2021; Kvedaraite et al., 2021; Affandi et al., 2021), it appears that DC3 may be depleted during severe infection.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from cited studies on DC3 in SARS-CoV-2 infection.

claim: It is plausible that DC3 may be present in the nasopharynx during acute IAV infection.
source: As the pattern of overall DC depletion from circulation is shared between IAV and SARS-CoV-2 infections, it is plausible that DC3 may be present in the nasopharynx during acute IAV infection.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on similarities between IAV and SARS-CoV-2.

claim: Monocytes present in/recruited to the nasopharynx likely contribute to sustained DC recruitment by secreting TNFα, CCL2, CCL3, and CCL7 locally.
source: During acute disease, monocytes present in/recruited to the nasopharynx likely contribute to sustained DC recruitment by secreting TNFα, CCL2, CCL3, and CCL7 locally (Oshansky et al., 2014; Gill et al., 2008; Marion et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an inference supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Lower expression of CD86 on circulating myeloid cells as compared to nasopharyngeal cells during IAV infection suggests migration of mature cells to the nasopharynx, and/or in situ differentiation of monocytes to induced DCs in blood during acute IAV infection.
source: Lower expression of CD86 on circulating myeloid cells as compared to nasopharyngeal cells during IAV infection suggests migration of mature cells to the nasopharynx, and/or in situ differentiation of monocytes to induced DCs (that may not upregulate maturation markers) in blood during acute IAV infection as previously speculated (Cao et al., 2012).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the maturation marker data supported by a citation.

claim: In IAV infection, monocytes and DCs are likely recruited to the nasopharynx for a shorter period of time, where they face a similar fate (as in chronic SIV infection).
